payload.text: (hv, 2026-11-19, first-hand in prose in vc's session, read by 08:52Z on vc's date -u, and first-hand to ic and dc in their own sessions, relayed by each and read by 08:49Z and 08:50Z on their date -u; the four questions' wording is vc's, and every answer is hv's own words) IDS GO FROM ORDINALS TO GIT-STYLE IDS, UNIQUE BY CONSTRUCTION, AT P0. vc asked: (1) git-style ids for new threads and issues, (2) everywhere or only where a project turns it on, (3) work packages too, (4) anything sooner for the cohort. hv: "1: Yes 2: Everywhere, going forward 3: My instinct is to do the same thing there, for consistency, no? 4: No, let's do this now". Then: "On reflection, we need this on STs, WPs, and ISSUEs. And then ordering needs to be date/time based as the default, rather than ordinally by ST, WP or Issue number". On a stop-gap that would let an issue be created only on main: "that is pants. We can't have that restriction". To ic and dc: "We need to go all-in a fix to ST, WP, and ISSUE numbering (from ordinals to git-style hashes based on the guid of the creation event). This is a P0 fix that needs to be done asap. Please hold for further instructions from VC." PROCESS, hv to vc: "I want this documented as a new steel thread with elaborated WPs no, in Fable mode before we write a line of code. When the ST and WPs are done, I will review before we kick off the work (I'll start the other Claudes here to do it)." So ST0095 is written first, and no code lands on it before hv has reviewed it. This reverses the rejection of a change to the minting scheme in ST0078's design of 2026-09-18. "Going forward" leaves every existing id as it is. The trigger: merge request 8 on an attendee's practice repository, where one person with five merge requests open met a collision on every mint.
